entity.description: A vault (§3.1). Its kind (VaultKind: personal or operational) and lock (VaultLock: single-secret or shared-key) are chosen when it is made and never change. keyVersion is the vault key's current version, which a removal rotates; revision goes up with each change of the member list or key, and a change names the revision it was made from (a compare-and-swap, decision (a) of §9). A single-secret vault holds its wrapped vault key (secretWrap, with its KDF parameters) and has no members and no recovery. A personal vault's name is in headerCipher, sealed by the vault key in the client; an operational vault's vaultName is in the clear, with its deposit key (V2). recoveryOn: the organization's recovery key wraps the vault key (V4); an operational vault keeps recovery on or two members.

field.name: ownerUserId
field.description: Who made it; a single-secret vault's only user

field.name: vaultName
field.description: Operational vaults only, in the clear

field.name: headerCipher
field.description: A personal vault's header (its name), sealed in the client

field.name: secretKindEnumId
field.description: Single-secret: a password or a generated key (VaultSecretKind)

field.name: secretWrap
field.description: Single-secret: the vault key wrapped by the password (Argon2id) or the generated key (HKDF), as the vault crate's JSON with its parameters

field.name: depositPublic
field.description: Operational (V2): the deposit key's public half

field.name: depositKeyVersion
field.description: The key version the deposit key was made for, as signed

field.name: depositWrappedPrivate
field.description: The deposit key's private half, wrapped by the vault key

field.name: lastOpenedDate
field.description: A single-secret vault's last open the client reported, for the reminder of §3.11

entity.description: One signed entry of a vault's member-list chain (§3.9, crates/moqui-vault keyversion.rs): a key version and a revision of its member list (an add is the next revision of the same version, a removal revision 1 of the next version). memberList is the members as signed (each user, role, personal key id and public keys, as JSON), and the signer held the manage role in the entry before (the first: the maker, a manager in it). A client accepts a key version only through this chain, back to a signer whose key its user checked.

A member's wrap of one key version of a vault key, to their personal key, with who made it and their signature (§3.9). The rows of the vault's current keyVersion are its members, with their role (VaultMemberRole: manage, write and read for a personal vault, manage, approve and reveal for an operational one), which the services enforce. A rotation writes each remaining member's wrap of the new version and keeps their earlier ones until they open the new version (ack#VaultKeyVersion, decision (b) of §9); a removed member's rows are all deleted.

field.name: wrappedVaultKey
field.description: HPKE to the member's personal key

field.name: ackedDate
field.description: When the member opened this version

entity.description: One item of a vault, its own random item key wrapped by the vault key (itemKeyWrapEnumId VwVault) or, for an item the server deposits into an operational vault, to the deposit key (VwDeposit, V2). The body is the item's JSON, sealed whole by the item key. keyVersion is the version the item key is wrapped under; a write is taken only at the vault's current version, and names the revision it was made from. A personal vault's row holds no name, type or value in the clear: they are in the body. An operational item also has its type, binding and name in the clear (all three in the associated data), and bindingKey is unique in its vault.

field.name: itemKeyVersion
field.description: The key version the item key was made at; a rotation rewraps the item key (keyVersion) and leaves this, so the item's first write after a key-version change makes a new item key (decision (c) of §9)

field.name: vaultItemTypeId
field.description: Operational only

field.name: bindingKey
field.description: Operational only: AppInstance:<id>:dbPassword

field.name: itemName
field.description: Operational only

entity.description: An earlier revision of an item, with its wrapped key and body as they were: a password's history, and a rotation's way back (§4.7). Written by update#VaultItem; kept for a retention period.

A user's personal key (§3.5): an X25519 key pair to receive wraps and an Ed25519 key pair to sign. The public halves are in the clear; the two private halves are wrapped together by the key passphrase (Argon2id, its parameters in the wrap) and by the user's recovery code. The server keeps no hash of either and sends the wraps only to their own user after a strong, recent sign-in (vault@key-fetch-max-age). A user has one key with status VpkActive; replacing it marks the old one VpkReplaced, and nothing is wrapped to the new key until its fingerprint is checked again.

field.name: passphraseWrap
field.description: The vault crate's password wrap, as JSON

entity.description: A key a user checked by comparing its fingerprint (§3.5): the checker and their personal key, the checked key (a personalKeyId with both its public halves, or lease-key: the server's lease key, V2), when (checkedAt, epoch millis, as signed) and the checker's signature. A client verifies the signature with its own key before it relies on the check; a check is for one key, so a changed key is checked again.

field.name: checkedUserId
field.description: The user whose key the checker compared it with, as signed; empty for the lease key

entity.description: An organization's recovery key (§3.10, V4): its public halves (X25519 to wrap to and Ed25519 to sign, the vault crate's 64 bytes as hex), signed by the holder who made it (makerUserId, makerKeyId), split k of n across its holders (Shamir, decision of §9), kept by user group or by instance. A vault with recovery on lists it as a member with the manage role, under the user id recovery:recoveryKeyId; thruDate ends it for new vaults.

field.name: sharesNeeded
field.description: k

field.name: sharesTotal
field.description: n

field.name: usedDate
field.description: When a recovery used it: the recovering holder's client held the whole key then (the limit of Shamir, §3.12), so each vault that lists it replaces it with a new one

entity.description: A holder's share of a recovery key (V4), sealed to their personal key and signed by its maker.

A recovery under way (§3.10, V4): the ephemeral public key the recovering holder's client made and keeps the private half of in memory, the vault, the member and their new personal key the vault key is to be wrapped to, all signed by the recovering holder (holderUserId, with holderKeyId) as the vault crate's RecoverySession. The other holders seal their shares to the ephemeral key (VaultRecoveryDelivery); the recovering client combines k of them and completes the recovery (statusId VrsCompleted), or it is cancelled or runs out (VrsCancelled). A vault with recovery on lists its recovery key as a member (recovery:recoveryKeyId), whose wrap the recovery opens.

field.name: subjectUserId
field.description: The member recovered

field.name: subjectKeyId
field.description: Their new personal key

field.name: expiresAt
field.description: Epoch millis: a day after it started, no share is taken and it does not complete

entity.description: One holder's share sealed to a recovery session's ephemeral key and signed by the holder (V4), as the vault crate's SessionShare. Only the session's ephemeral key, in the recovering holder's client, opens it.

A value sealed to one user's personal key (HPKE), from a user (senderKind user: their signing key, senderKeyId the personal key the server checked the signature with) or an instance (instance: its link key, M6), with its purpose and the sender's signature (§3.3). Only the recipient lists it; their client checks the signature and files the value into a vault (filedDate).

A lease (§3.7, V2): the vault, the items it names (each id, type, binding and name, as JSON), the operation, the cluster member that runs it, the lease's ephemeral public key and the time limit, signed by the server's lease key; once approved, the item keys sealed to the lease's key, with the approver and their signature. It never holds a key that opens anything by itself.

field.name: expiresAt
field.description: Epoch millis, as signed

field.name: approverKeyId
field.description: The approver's personal key the approval signature was checked with

field.name: machineAccess
field.description: Y: opened under an environment's machine access, approved by "machine"

field.name: environmentId
field.description: The environment of a machine-access lease, or of a lease asked to grant machine access

entity.description: An environment's machine access to one item (§3.8, V2): its item key sealed by the vault crate's AEAD under the server's machine key, with the environment, vault and item ids as associated data. The column is not an entity encrypt="true" field, so no find, cache, export or sync decrypts it.

field.name: staleDate
field.description: When the item was written with a new item key, which this sealed key no longer opens: a lease under it is refused until machine access is given again

entity.description: A desktop or mobile app that remembers its user's open personal key for a time (§3.5, V5). The key stays on the device, wrapped by a key in its own key store; this row holds none of it, only that the device remembers it, for which personal key, and until when. The device asks for its row before it opens the key from memory, so a row deleted here (the user took the device off the list) or past its time is a memory that does not open again. The user's Vault key settings list them (list#VaultDeviceMemories).

field.name: deviceMemoryId
field.description: The device's id of the memory, which is in the wrap's associated data

field.name: thruStamp
field.description: When the memory ends, epoch millis

entity.description: An event of §3.13 (VaultEventType), written in the transaction of the change it records: a vault made or deleted, a wrapped key fetched, a member added or removed, a key rotation, a delivery sent or filed, and the later phases' leases, machine access, recoveries and reveals. userId acted; subjectUserId is whom it was about (the member, the recipient). detail is words, never a key or a value. Kept as long as the audit log; a deleted vault's events stay.

An item type (§3.4): the client draws an item's form from its fields, and the server checks an operational item's shape when it uses it. The framework's are seed data (VaultTypeData.xml); a component adds its own (an instance kind's items).
A field of an item type: its label, its kind (VaultFieldKind: text, secret, URL, TOTP, multi-line, date, file name) and whether its value is masked until asked for.
